headlines.description: Democrat Scott Colom’s upset victory in Mississippi’s U.S. Senate race is drawing new scrutiny to the state’s unusual election laws, which make it harder for some voters to cast ballots. Mississippi law can prevent voters from casting a normal ballot after election officials receive information suggesting they have moved, even if the information hasn’t been verified.
